note: User Redirect redirects users after login/logout to a per-role internal/external URL. All state lives in the schema-less config object user_redirect.settings (login.<role>.redirect_url + weight, logout.<role>.redirect_url + weight, ignore[], ignore_for{login,logout}); there is no config/install file so the object does not exist until the settings form is saved. Baseline on this site = config absent. Medium cases write known keys and read them back; hard cases delete the config (verify FAILS on the empty baseline) and require the agent to set the right key. Roles present on this site: anonymous, authenticated, content_editor, administrator.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site I enabled the user_redirect module. Where do I configure where users go after login/logout, and where is that stored in config?
evals.expected_output: Configure it on the settings form at /admin/people/users/redirect/form/settings (route user_redirect.settings, permission 'administer user redirect settings'). Values are stored in the user_redirect.settings config object under login.<role_id>.redirect_url/weight and logout.<role_id>.redirect_url/weight, plus ignore[] and ignore_for.

evals.prompt: How does the user_redirect module actually perform the redirect for an internal path versus an external URL after login, and how does it choose when a user has several roles?
evals.expected_output: For an internal path it sets the request's 'destination' query parameter (core then redirects there); for an external URL (UrlHelper::isExternal) it sends a TrustedRedirectResponse immediately. When the user has several roles it reverses the roles and applies the first role that has a non-empty redirect_url (last role in the account's list wins).

evals.prompt: The user_redirect module has an 'Ignore paths' setting. What path does it ignore by default and why does that matter?
evals.expected_output: The default ignore list contains /user/reset/* so that one-time login / password-reset links are not hijacked by the redirect. The ignore check runs only when ignore_for.login (or .logout) is enabled, matching the current path's alias against the patterns.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site already has the user_redirect module configured. Inspect the live configuration and tell me where a user with the 'administrator' role will be redirected after they log in.
evals.expected_output: The administrator role's login redirect is /admin/content (user_redirect.settings login.administrator.redirect_url = /admin/content).

evals.prompt: On this site, user_redirect is configured to skip the redirect on certain paths for login. Inspect the live configuration and list the ignore path patterns that are in effect.
evals.expected_output: The ignore list is /user/reset/* and /promo/*, applied for login (user_redirect.settings ignore = [/user/reset/*, /promo/*], ignore_for.login enabled).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the user_redirect module to configure that users with the 'administrator' role are redirected to /admin/content immediately after they log in. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set user_redirect.settings login.administrator.redirect_url to /admin/content (via the settings form at /admin/people/users/redirect/form/settings or drush config).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want every logged-in (authenticated) user to be sent to the home page when they log out. Set this up using the user_redirect module.
evals.expected_output: Set user_redirect.settings logout.authenticated.redirect_url to / (the front page) for the authenticated role.
